August Pfluger

Republican candidate for U.S. Representative, District 11, Travis County, Texas · Incumbent

U.S. Representative for Texas' 11th Congressional District; retired U.S. Air Force officer

August Pfluger is a Republican who has represented Texas' 11th Congressional District since January 2021 and chairs the Republican Study Committee. He won the Republican primary on March 3, 2026, and faces Democrat Claire Reynolds in the November 3, 2026 general election. He lives in San Angelo and served about two decades in the U.S. Air Force as an F-22 pilot.

Where Pfluger stands

Cost of living / affordability
Says affordability is his top legislative focus in 2026. Cites the Working Families Tax Cuts Act and says he wrote legislation to lower prescription drug prices.
Federal spending and debt
Says the One Big Beautiful Bill made the largest spending cut ever along with the largest tax cut in history. Supports auditing every federal agency, especially the Pentagon.
Energy / oil and gas
Says he has sponsored legislation to defend oil and gas production and worked to deregulate the industry. Says a free market for oil is important.
Data centers and AI
Supported the House-passed Ratepayer Protection Act. Prefers local decisions on data centers over one federal rule, and backs a light regulatory touch on AI so the U.S. can compete with China.
Tariffs and trade
Says free trade requires fair trade. Supports President Trump's tariffs as holding countries such as Brazil and Canada accountable.
Immigration / ICE
Says he has voted every time to fund ICE and pledges continued support for Customs and Border Protection and ICE. Says he opposes open-border policies.
Iran
Says Iran can never have a nuclear weapon. Supports the administration's military campaign against Iran.
Ukraine / NATO
Says he believes in peace through strength and that appeasement does not work. Notes Ukraine is not a NATO ally and says he will always vote to fund the military.
Surveillance cameras / privacy
Says Congress should protect privacy and that decisions on license-plate cameras belong to state and local governments. Says he has voted every year to increase law-enforcement funding.
Daylight saving time
Has voted for permanent daylight saving time.

Background

  • U.S. Representative, Texas District 11, 2021–present
  • Chairman, Republican Study Committee, 2025–present
  • Member, House Homeland Security and Energy and Commerce committees
  • Served on the National Security Council
  • U.S. Air Force, about two decades (he has also cited 26 years); F-22 pilot; retired as a Lt. Colonel per his questionnaire
  • Education: U.S. Air Force Academy (student-athlete)
  • Graduate of San Angelo Central High School
